successors.name: Republic of Chile
successors.text: the Mapuche lands south of the Biobío: 'Chile finally achieved the occupation and integration of the territories south of the Biobío River in 1884'

successors.name: Argentine Confederation
successors.text: Puelmapu, 'a land comprising part of the Argentine pampa and Patagonia', conquered in the Conquest of the Desert, whose last battle was fought on 18 October 1884

ledger.x: 1810: the dossier begins with the independent Mapuche country as Chile's first fifty years of independence leave it alone.
December 1861: Chile builds its first fort on Mapuche land.
1862: Chile takes Angol and the Biobío-Malleco strip.
1862: the Angol advance ends the first contest; Chile holds the strip from now on.
1868: Chilean operations resume against the Mapuche south of the Malleco.
1871: Quilapán is repulsed at the Malleco line and the fighting stops.
December 1878: Roca's first sweep clashes with the Mapuche at Lihué Calel.
1879: Roca's second sweep reaches the Río Negro.
January 1881: the Mapuche of the Malleco zone rise.
1881: Chile takes the Malleco-Cautín country after the January rising.
1882: Chilean forts in the Andean valleys.
1 January 1883: Chile refounds Villarrica and the occupation of the Araucanía ends.
18 October 1884: the Conquest of the Desert fights its last battle.
1884: the last free Mapuche land passes to Argentina.
1884: the last free Mapuche communities surrender.

wars.name: Occupation of Araucanía
wars.outcome: Chilean victory: the Malleco line (1862-1871), then Temuco and Victoria (1881), then Villarrica refounded on 1 January 1883; 'Today the whole Araucanía is subjugated' (1 June 1883).

wars.name: Conquest of the Desert
wars.outcome: Argentine victory: the 'Argentine annexation of Patagonia', the last battle on 18 October 1884.

wars.name: Kingdom of Araucanía and Patagonia (Orélie-Antoine de Tounens)
wars.outcome: No territorial result: Tounens declared the kingdom 'by two ordinances on November 17, 1860 and November 20, 1860', was 'arrested on January 5, 1862' and 'expelled to France on October 28, 1862'.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is dated on the pages opened; the Biobío (to 1861), the Malleco line (1862-1880), the Cautín line (1881) and the Río Negro-Neuquén line (1879) are approximate river-and-fort frontiers.
